summary: Today’s pulse tracks Lib Dems use conference to set out £2bn plan to cut fuel duty, Victoria Starmer models clothes at London fashion week show, and Trump says his D.C. arch will serve as 'military complex' with snipers and drones. Across Guardian and NPR, the strongest repeated signals are party, mental, and starmer. In the background, One Nation-linked company built $56,000 shed on private property of Pauline Hanson’s right-hand man and Adults with severe mental illness die 15 to 20 years earlier from diseases such as cancer keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Lib Dems use conference to set out £2bn plan to cut fuel duty
headlines.description: Ed Davey’s party made a series of proposals as concern grows among members that voters don’t know what its policies are or what it stands for The Liberal Democrats have used their conference to unveil a £2bn plan to cut fuel duty, part of a series of policy proposals intended to tackle worries that not enough voters know what Ed Davey ’s party stands for. The proposal to cut fuel duty by 10p a litre for a fixed three-month period came as polling showed Lib Dem policies are less well known than those of Restore Britain , which only launched as a political party in February and has one MP – Rupert Lowe – to their 71.

headlines.title: Victoria Starmer models clothes at London fashion week show
headlines.description: Wife of former PM takes part in designer Edeline Lee’s show inspired by the Greek myth of Sisyphus Victoria Starmer has taken part in a London fashion week show, in one of her first public appearances since her husband, Keir Starmer, stepped down as prime minister. Lady Starmer appeared at Sunday’s Edeline Lee show. The London-based, Canadian British designer’s clothes are a favourite of the Princess of Wales, and have also been worn by celebrities including singer Taylor Swift and actor and screenwriter Phoebe Waller-Bridge.

headlines.title: Trump says his D.C. arch will serve as 'military complex' with snipers and drones
headlines.description: President Trump has claimed that military operations are needed at his proposed triumphal arch in Washington D.C., in order to protect national security. A federal court is weighing the arch's legality.

headlines.title: One Nation-linked company built $56,000 shed on private property of Pauline Hanson’s right-hand man
headlines.description: Exclusive: James Ashby also drives new Ford Ranger given to party and is main pilot of plane donated by Gina Rinehart, which he says are not for personal use Guardian Australia understands that Ashby, formerly Hanson’s chief of staff and now the party’s national director, also drives a new Ford Ranger that was “personally” gifted to One Nation by Hancock Agriculture’s chief executive, Adam Giles, in April. Hanson said the vehicle would help the party’s campaign efforts and “provides us the presence we need in the lead-up to the next federal election”. headlines.title: Adults with severe mental illness die 15 to 20 years earlier from diseases such as cancer
headlines.description: Exclusive: Stark health inequalities in terms of deaths before age of 75, NHS data reveals Adults with severe mental illness are nearly five times more likely than their peers to die from serious physical diseases before the age of 75, according to research. The analysis of NHS data by the Rethink Mental Illness charity reveals that people with severe mental health problems die 15-20 years earlier than the wider adult population, largely due to preventable physical conditions.

headlines.title: Ukraine targets Moscow with hundreds of drones on final day of Russian election
headlines.description: At least three people killed and oil refinery damaged as doubts cast over initial reports of ballistic missile use Ukraine has targeted Moscow and the surrounding region in a large-scale attack that involved hundreds of drones. The attack killed at least three people and damaged what Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said was one of Russia’s “key oil industry facilities” on the final day of the country’s parliamentary elections , authorities said on Sunday.

headlinePool.title: Meta launches legal challenge against UK media regulator over Online Safety Act
headlinePool.description: Action against Ofcom comes as social media companies are being accused of using courts to slow down implementation Meta has launched a fresh legal challenge against Britain’s media regulator in the latest of a slew of actions by social media companies who are accused of using the courts to slow down implementation of the Online Safety Act. Lawyers for the parent company of Facebook served notice during the week in an appeal against placing WhatsApp and Instagram, which are also owned by Meta, in a category that subjects them to additional duties.

headlinePool.title: Bear-y good neighbors: humans and animals are learning to live together in an expanding LA
headlinePool.description: People are increasingly crossing paths with the wild animals as homes ring the outskirts of forests, sparking a new era of coexistence Every year, as summer draws to a close and fall begins, California’s bears get hungry. Black bears have long roamed the state, hunting for acorns, ants and pine nuts by the bucketload to pack on calories before hibernation. But increasingly, for every berry and root, there’s an even greater temptation: our trash and the detritus of human existence.

headlinePool.title: Trump says his planned triumphal arch will double as a military complex to store ammunition
headlinePool.description: Trump said the updated plans were at the request of the US military and for national security purposes.

headlinePool.title: Trump claims triumphal arch will serve as a ‘top grade military complex’ to store weapons
headlinePool.description: US president on Truth Social claims his new plan for the 250ft arch comes at the ‘strong request’ of the US military Donald Trump is proffering a new argument for building his triumphal arch in Washington DC: it will be converted into a “top grade military complex” replete with drone and ammunition storage space and customised sniper facilities on the roof and plaza. In a post on his Truth Social platform on Sunday morning, Trump claimed that his new plan came at the “strong request” of the US military. He said the 250ft structure would be able to “house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage”.

headlinePool.title: UK startup snares $20m to recreate gigs with ‘hyper-realistic’ digital avatars
headlinePool.description: Unit1 hopes to offer lower cost version of shows such as Abba Voyage, showcasing living and dead artists in any venue The former chief executive of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s entertainment group has obtained a near-£15m investment for his UK music tech startup that hopes to recreate classic concerts by manifesting musicians as digital avatars. Unit1 was set up last year by Barney Wragg, an entertainment executive who ran Lord Lloyd-Webber’s Cats-to-Evita empire for five years from late 2011. It has secured the $20m in funding from a group of investors, including tech backer Balderton Capital through its partner Daniel Waterhouse, who made early investments in Spotify.

headlinePool.title: PHOTOS: The precarious life of fisherfolk
headlinePool.description: In the bustling heart of the southern Indian city of Chennai is a market that never sleeps, where residents from the poorest neighborhoods wage a battle of survival with the sea.

headlinePool.title: Michelle Bachelet withdraws from race to become UN secretary general
headlinePool.description: Former president of Chile drops out after support collapsed in security council straw poll, leaving seven candidates in contest Michelle Bachelet, a former president of Chile, has withdrawn her candidacy to become the next secretary general of the ⁠UN, ending an attempt ​that had struggled to gain traction among security council members. Bachelet, 74, announced ⁠her decision in a video posted on Instagram on Saturday, saying: “I will now continue, with the ⁠same determination as always, my international work.”

headlinePool.title: ‘I have nothing in the UK at all’: British man torn from his Swedish wife and home
headlinePool.description: Charles lands at Heathrow with just two bags and nowhere to go as a result of Brexit and Stockholm’s hardline immigration position Doubled over a Heathrow baggage trolley, the former British business director is sobbing uncontrollably, exhausted emotionally and physically after being deported from Sweden. Hours earlier the 65-year-old had been marched on to a plane in Stockholm, separated from his home and his Swedish wife after a five-year battle to stay in the country after Brexit came to an end.

headlinePool.title: Rabies concerns grow in the US – but it’s unclear if there’s an increase of the fatal disease
headlinePool.description: Rabid goats at a North Carolina petting zoo and a diseased beaver attacking a Maryland boy have set the public on edge Recent unusual incidents involving humans and rabid animals and a subsequent Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) advisory have prompted concerns about rabies, but it’s not clear if there has actually been an increase in cases of the deadly disease in the United States, experts say. In recent months, rabid beavers have attacked three people in Maryland , and hundreds of people were exposed to goats with rabies at a petting zoo in North Carolina , according to news reports. The CDC issued a health advisory on 10 September “in response to recent reports of increases in human exposures to rabid or possibly rabid animals”.
